title: And Now, My Soul, Another Year
description: And Now, My Soul, Another Year in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Simon Browne wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 895 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Closing Year”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: And now, my soul, an-oth-er year Of my short life is past: I can-not long con-tin-ue here; And this may be my last.

lines: And now, my soul, another year
Of my short life is past:
I cannot long continue here;
And this may be my last.
Part of my doubtful life is gone,
Nor will return again;
And swift my fleeting moments run —
The few which yet remain!
Awake, my soul! with all thy care
Thy true condition learn;
What are thy hopes — how sure, how fair,
And what thy great concern?
Now a new space of life begins,
Set out afresh for heaven;
Seek pardon for thy former sins,
Through Christ, so freely given.
Devoutly yield thyself to God,
And on his grace depend;
With zeal pursue the heavenly road,
Nor doubt a happy end.

licence: Public domain: Simon Browne died in 1732.
credits: Words by Simon Browne (1680–1732), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
